title: Present schedule dates as strict dd/mm/yyyy inputs

evidence: Fresh authenticated SSR and Chrome 151 rendered the intended source pattern as [0-9]2/[0-9]2/[0-9]4; valid 29/02/2028 and 31/12/2028 values converted to canonical ISO Form Data/draft JSON but failed native constraint validation, so the visible controls do not accept valid strict dd/mm/yyyy input.

Malformed, impossible, and incomplete input received an explicit invalid state and never reached Form Data/localStorage as a non-ISO literal; ISO draft restoration passed. Focused 4/4, full 119/119, check, build, diff-check, and hard-boundary review passed but do not overturn the observed valid-input failure.

Fresh authenticated SSR and hydrated Chrome 151 rendered both strict patterns exactly; valid 29/02/2028 and 31/12/2028 passed native constraint validation and produced canonical ISO Form Data plus the exact ISO-only scoped draft JSON.

Malformed, impossible, and incomplete values were visibly invalid and supplied no non-ISO Form Data/storage value; ISO draft restoration passed. Focused 5/5, full 120/120, check, build, diff-check, and forbidden-scope review passed.

purpose: Make recurring-schedule date entry strict and understandable for users while preserving the existing ISO request, storage, and scheduling contracts.
success_outcome: The Admin schedule form presents and validates strict dd/mm/yyyy start/end values, converts valid values to canonical ISO YYYY-MM-DD Form Data, and leaves the existing center/class-scoped ISO draft JSON unchanged.
anti_goals: Do not change Center & Scheduling date validation, recurrence, zero-occurrence rejection, Schedule/Lesson persistence, or the existing invalid_schedule envelope.
Do not change the study-calendar:schedule-draft:${centerId}:${classId} key, whitelist, ISO storage representation, or success/failure cleanup behavior.
Do not add a dependency, server route, server parser, calendar/lesson-context UI, authentication behavior, or FT-003 fixture work.

stop_conditions: Stop if strict dd/mm/yyyy input cannot preserve canonical ISO Form Data and the existing draft JSON without changing a server or storage boundary.
Stop if invalid or impossible dates cannot be rejected without changing Center & Scheduling validation or the existing schedule error contract.
Stop if implementation requires changing the protected Admin route's server load/action, adding a dependency, or touching FT-003/lesson-context behavior.

constraints: Use the existing Admin schedule form and preserve ordinary form submission; valid user text dd/mm/yyyy must become the same ISO YYYY-MM-DD values consumed by the existing action.
Keep storage/browser lifecycle SSR-safe and serialize only the existing startDate, endDate, and weekdays whitelist under the existing center/class key.
Keep the current calendar, schedule lifecycle, authorization, and zero-occurrence behavior unchanged.
invariants: A valid dd/mm/yyyy date maps to exactly one canonical ISO YYYY-MM-DD wire/storage value; no locale-dependent value reaches the server or draft storage.
Malformed, impossible, or incomplete dates remain visibly invalid and cannot submit a non-ISO value.
Existing draft isolation, failure retention, successful cleanup, and SSR safety remain unchanged.
verification_targets: FT-002-AC-010 / REQ-004: focused SSR/source and browser/form checks prove strict dd/mm/yyyy presentation and malformed/impossible-date rejection, while valid entry submits the unchanged ISO YYYY-MM-DD Form Data.

Regression: the existing AC-008 draft test proves the study-calendar:schedule-draft:${centerId}:${classId} key and exact ISO JSON whitelist remain unchanged; npm run check, npm run test, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
Boundary review: source/diff inspection confirms no Admin server action, Center & Scheduling module, persistence, calendar/lesson-context route, dependency, or FT-003 fixture changes.
